operatorApproval.notes: Worker pane v01 (pane w8:p16, metabolomics/qwen3.8-flash_next) on base 9cf164fa (the H01-H07 evidence commit in berlinguyinca/pi-engineering), isolated-change mode, first pass, ~5 min. Exactly the two declared files (git show --name-only HEAD: test/fixtures/harness-drift/README.md, test/fixtures/harness-drift/tasks.json), 95 changed lines against the 100 isolated-change ceiling, and no production file touched. Conductor verified independently at 67a27366: the fixture parses as JSON with exactly 5 tasks (drift-01..drift-05); git diff --check 9cf164fa..HEAD exit 0. The answer key was recomputed from the actions rather than trusted: for every task except the one documented case the first kind=change action outside permittedScope equals drift.expectedFirstViolationSeq, and the two clean controls (drift-01, drift-05) carry no out-of-scope change and expect null, so a scope-only detector scores 4 of 5 and the fixture still discriminates. The deliberate exception is drift-03, whose planted violation (seq 3, src/ledger/claimDiscipline.ts) sits INSIDE permittedScope and is keyed unrelated because it is off-objective; README.md's per-id table states this, so the fixture also proves a detector must reason about relevance and not only paths. Identical-snapshot clause verified mechanically: 3 distinct snapshot serialisations across 5 tasks, i.e. drift-01/drift-02 and drift-04/drift-05 hold byte-identical snapshots, so a detector cannot separate those pairs by snapshot alone; every task opens with legitimate reads inside its own permittedScope, which is the false-positive probe the delta asked for. README.md disclaims that the fixture asserts nothing about real model quality, and the file carries no absolute paths, secrets or run-varying values (no Date anywhere).
